L9: # Reporting Safety Concerns at an Encampment
L10: 
L11: Contact us about dangerous health and safety conditions at an encampment in Berkeley.
L12: ## Call or report online
L13: 
L14: Call (510) 981-2489 or submit a 【5†service request†berkeleyca.qscend.com】 if you have non-emergency concerns about unsafe conditions on a street or sidewalk in Berkeley. Examples may include:
L15: 
L16:   * Health hazards, such as human waste, syringes, or rodents
L17:   * Obstruction of sidewalks or roadways
L18:   * Interference with business or residence
L19:   * Large accumulation of belongings or debris
L20: In case of an emergency, non-emergency crime, or to receive homeless services, please contact the appropriate number below:
L21: 
L22:   * Contact 911 for emergencies such as fire, violent crime, or medical emergency.
L23:   * Contact (510) 981-5900 for non-emergency police response to nonviolent crimes such as theft.
L24:   * Contact 211 to get connected with 【6†homeless services】, such as shelter, housing, and referrals to services.
L25: If you were living in an encampment and the City is storing your belongings, you can contact 311 to make an appointment to recover your items. Read the City's policies about 【7†storing personal property】 (Administrative Regulation 10.1) and 【8†objects on sidewalks】 (Administrative Regulation 10.2).
L26: ## Assessment is the first step
L27: 
L28: After you report your concern to 311, the Homeless Response Team will assess the site for its impacts. Among the factors the City looks at are:
L29: 
L30:   * Fire and safety hazards
L31:   * Health hazards
L32:   * Environmental hazards
L33:   * Obstruction of the public right-of-way
L34:   * Interference with businesses, residences, public infrastructure, or construction
L35:   * City resources for outreach and intervention
L36:   * Shelter availability
L37:   * Legal issues
L38: After assessment, the Homeless Response Team’s next steps depend on circumstances. The team performs direct outreach to connect residents with shelter or housing, as well as improve cleanliness at the encampment. They also coordinate service delivery with nonprofit partners and other City departments.
L39: 
L40: Ultimately, the unit’s main goal is to reduce harms and resolve issues in a meaningful manner.
L41: ## Homeless Response Team Performance Data Report
L42: 
L43: The Homeless Response Team reports regularly on performance data, including participant demographics and placements into shelter. Read recent reports:
L44: 
L45:   * 【9†June 2026 Performance Data Report】
L46:   * 【10†November 2025 Performance Data Report】
L47:   * 【11†May 2025 Performance Data Report】

L8@P1: Background
L9@P1: The mission of the Berkeley City Auditor is to promote transparency and accountability. Each audit report we
L10@P1: issue includes recommendations for how the audited department can serve Berkeley residents more equitably,
L11@P1: efficiently, and effectively. Following up on audit recommendations helps hold departments accountable for
L12@P1: implementing the improvements they agreed to. Additional up-to-date information on each audit
L13@P1: recommendation is available on our online dashboard on our website.
L14@P1: Implementation Status of Recommendations
L15@P1: In our last audit follow-up report on December 19, 2024, there were 58 open recommendations. Since then, we
L16@P1: have issued one performance audit which added six new recommendations and a follow-up report which reopened eight recommendations from the 2009 Leases Audit.
L17@P1: Figure 1. There are currently 48 open audit recommendations across 4 departments as well as
L18@P1: the Mayor and City Council.
L19@P1: Source: Auditor’s Analysis
L20@P1: Management has continued to make progress towards implementing open audit recommendations across 10
L21@P1: audits. During this reporting period, management has implemented 23 of the outstanding recommendations.
L22@P1: However, the Berkeley Public Library dropped one partly implemented recommendation because it passed the
L23@P1: five-year mark. This recommendation was the final outstanding recommendation from the 2020 Berkeley
L24@P1: Public Library audit, so our office formally closed this audit.
L25@P1: Figure 2. Departments implemented 23 recommendations during this reporting period.
L26@P1: Note: This reporting period covers November 7, 2024 through September 24, 2025.

L40@P2: We use the following statuses to report on the implementation of audit recommendations:
L41@P2: Implemented Auditee has completely implemented the recommendations.
L42@P2: Partially Implemented Auditee has implemented 50 percent or more of the recommendation.
L43@P2: Started Auditee has started to address the recommendation but has not reached the
L44@P2: 50 percent threshold.
L45@P2: Not Started Auditee has not yet taken action to implement the recommendation.
L46@P2: Dropped Auditee has accepted the risk to the city that the recommendation is meant to
L47@P2: address and is unable or unwilling to implement the recommendation.
L48@P2: Additionally, all open recommendations will be reported as dropped if they are
L49@P2: not implemented within five years of audit issuance.1

L119@P4: To: Honorable Mayor and Members of the City Council
L120@P4: From: Jenny Wong, City Auditor
L121@P4: Subject: 2025 Audit Follow-up Status Update
L122@P4: INTRODUCTION
L123@P4: This item provides a status update on the audit follow-up of all recommendations since our last
L124@P4: report on December 19, 2024. Administrative regulations require the City Auditor to monitor
L125@P4: the status of outstanding audit recommendations and periodically report to City Council.
L126@P4: CURRENT SITUATION AND ITS EFFECTS
L127@P4: We follow up on audits to assess whether city departments implemented the audit
L128@P4: recommendations. The Auditor’s Office issues annual follow-up audit reports to City Council on
L129@P4: the status of our recommendations.
L130@P4: As of October 28, 2025, there are currently 48 open recommendations across 4 departments as
L131@P4: well as the Mayor and City Council. We additionally marked 23 outstanding audit
L132@P4: recommendations as implemented this cycle. Departments have implemented 45 of the 94 (48
L133@P4: percent) audit recommendations released since 2020.
L134@P4: 1 Compared to the last follow-up period’s
L135@P4: implementation rate of 37 percent, the rate has increased by 11 percentage points.
L136@P4: Figure 1. There are currently 48 open recommendations across 4 departments as well as the
L137@P4: Mayor and City Council.
L138@P4: Source: Auditor’s analysis

L147@P5: During this audit follow-up cycle of November 7, 2024 to September 24, 2025, we closed 3 out
L148@P5: of 10 audits that were still open at the beginning of the period. Audits are closed when all
L149@P5: recommendations are implemented, or if they are older than five years. After five years,
L150@P5: recommendations that are not implemented are marked as “dropped” on the online dashboard.
L151@P5: This cycle, we closed the 2022 police overtime audit2 and the 2020 streets audit3 after the Police
L152@P5: Department and Public Works successfully implemented all remaining recommendations for
L153@P5: each audit. We also closed the 2020 Berkeley Public Library audit4 after all recommendations
L154@P5: were implemented except for one. We dropped the final recommendation because it passed the
L155@P5: five-year mark.
L156@P5: In this reporting period, Public Works provided their first update on our office’s follow-up
L157@P5: report on the 2009 audit of City leases,
L158@P5: 5 which was released in January of this year. Since
L159@P5: January, Public Works has started work on most of our recommendations. They now have a staff
L160@P5: member filling the role of Real Property Administrator who is working with an
L161@P5: interdepartmental team on a property management plan and leading the development of a
L162@P5: complete central inventory of leases and licenses.
L163@P5: The City Manager’s Office and Human Resources have made significant progress on the 2023
L164@P5: staff shortages audit.6 In this period, the City Manager and Human Resources have each
L165@P5: implemented 6 audit recommendations from this audit— bringing the overall number of
L166@P5: implemented recommendations from 3 to 15 (out of 25 total). For example, HR launched a
L167@P5: comprehensive training program for staff at all levels through NEOGOV Learn. This training
L168@P5: program includes the Supervisor Learning Plan, a hybrid experience for supervisors and

L187@P6: managers to learn how to be effective leaders in the City and support the overall City workforce.
L188@P6: Another accomplishment includes city management’s enhanced communication strategy,
L189@P6: including department open houses, a weekly wrap-up email to all staff, online town halls, and
L190@P6: annual manager meetings, to improve employee engagement.
L191@P6: Human Resources has also made strides on the 2019 domestic violence policy audit7 and
L192@P6: implemented 5 out of 6 total recommendations in this period alone. For example, HR recently
L193@P6: launched the updated Administrative Regulation 2.21 titled “Leave Policy for Absence Related to
L194@P6: Acts of Violence.” The new policy incorporates model policy elements and includes
L195@P6: comprehensive guidance for employees experiencing acts of violence.
L196@P6: The Health, Housing and Community Services’ (HHCS) Environmental Health Division
L197@P6: demonstrated progress on most recommendations from the 2024 restaurant inspections audit.8
L198@P6: According to the Division, all high and very high risk facilities that were not inspected in 2023
L199@P6: have now been inspected, and they have established a baseline inspection target of at least one
L200@P6: inspection per year per facility. However, the Division reversed their progress on one
L201@P6: recommendation after removing information about food inspections that was previously
L202@P6: provided on the City’s Open Data Portal. The Division is reportedly transitioning to an upgraded
L203@P6: database system and plans to enable public access to food facility inspection results, but the
L204@P6: timeline for implementation is unclear.
L205@P6: BACKGROUND
L206@P6: The City Auditor’s Office has a mission to promote transparency and accountability in Berkeley
L207@P6: government. We conduct independent performance audits to evaluate city operations and
L208@P6: programs and make recommendations to improve operations and services and ensure
L209@P6: productive use of taxpayer funds. We focus on equitable, efficient, and effective use of city
L210@P6: resources to achieve goals and objectives.
L211@P6: Following up on audit recommendations is an important part of the audit process that helps
L212@P6: hold departments accountable for implementing agreed-upon audit recommendations. To
L213@P6: further that goal, our office launched an online dashboard to track the status of outstanding
L214@P6: audit recommendations in September 2022. Additional up-to-date information on each audit
L215@P6: recommendation is available on our online dashboard on our website.
L216@P6: While we understand that some departments face staffing challenges that make it difficult to
L217@P6: prioritize audit recommendations, not implementing the recommendations can mean that the
L218@P6: City is not addressing the risks identified in audits or making needed improvements to
L219@P6: operations or services.

L225@P7: ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY AND CLIMATE IMPACTS
L226@P7: While there may be environmental impacts associated with some audit recommendations, there
L227@P7: are no identifiable environmental effects or opportunities associated with the audit follow-up
L228@P7: process.
